title.narrative: Enhancing resilience of vulnerable population through provision of Nutrition and Protection mainstreamed WASH Services in Bama LGA of Borno State.

description.narrative: ltpgtNortheast Nigeria is facing various challenges, including conflict, and natural disaster fuelling displacement, food insecurity, and epidemics, which contribute to the region's humanitarian needs. Insecurity, shortage of water and other basic needs along with disease outbreaks like diphtheria and cholera, have had significant impacts on the communities in the BAY states. Displacement remains a persistent issue due to the prolonged conflict between the Government and Non-State Armed Groups.ltbrgtDrawing from these data, this proposal aims to deliver life-saving WASH and multi-sectoral assistance to over 22,000 conflict-affected women, girls, boys, and men in Bama LGA, Borno State. The intervention targets IDPs in GSSSS Bama, Ngurosoye, returnees, and host communities, with the overarching goal of ensuring sustainable access to safe, adequate, and cost-effective WASH services that support health, dignity, and environmental stability. ltbrgtKey activities include mapping and risk assessment of WASH facilities in flood-prone and displacement-affected areas of Bama LGA, to identify vulnerabilities and inform targeted rehabilitation efforts. The project will rehabilitate, operate, and maintain 12 boreholes—comprising solar-powered motorized boreholes and hand pump boreholes. Water quality will be strictly monitored through chlorination and regular testing to meet recognized standards ranging from 0.3mg/l to 0.5mg/l, reducing the risk of waterborne diseases. In pursuance to an enhanced quality service delivery, 35 field staff and stakeholders, including Water point Chlorinators, CATI Team Members, Community Mobilisers, WASHCOMs, etc will receive training on effective WASH service delivery, water safety, and protective services such as PSEA and GBV mitigation best practices. Community-based structures, including WASH Committee members, will be equipped with tools and training to facilitate local operation and maintenance (VLOM), promoting ownership and sustainability beyond project completion. The proposal also targets to Rehabilitate 30 Blocks of Sanitation facilities in IDP Camps to argument for the recently decommissioned 31 blocks in GSSSS Camp including expediting effective daily Latrine cleaning and weekly environmental sanitation to mitigate environmental risk, while using the two Solid Waste Disposal Sites to be rehabilitated by the project. To complete the sanitation response loop, and making use of the LPF DSSU services, this proposal provides for Desludging services targeting 750 Dropholes/Stance of Latrine in flood prone areas of Bama LGA to mitigate environmental crises.ltbrgtOne CATI teams will be deployed in the case of Cholera/AWD Outbreak to activate Epidemiological Surveillance, Disinfection, Hygiene promotion activities, including Risk Communication and distribution of hygiene kits, targeting behavioral change, aiming for at improving safe hygiene practices to prevent spread of disease. The project also emphasizes the protection of women and girls, particularly through the facilitation of a GBV/SEA Safety Audit/Risk analyses where recommendations will be drawn and implemented, effectively tailored to ensure the safety of women and girls especially as it relates to water collection and sanitation facilities access. Overall, this integrated approach seeks not only to address immediate water and sanitation needs but also to strengthen local capacity, improve health outcomes, and promote resilience among vulnerable populations facing ongoing displacement, environmental hazards, and socio-economic challenges. Through collaboration with community stakeholders and partners. The project aspires to lay a foundation for sustainable WASH services that uphold human dignity and contribute to long-term recovery and stability in Bama LGA of Borno State, in the face of dwindling funding and uncertainties in the humanitarian response sphere.ltbrgtlt/pgt
